title: Ephemeral scale allocator + lane synchronizer for compact INT8 hotpath
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduces ephemeral scale allocator and lane synchronizer which reduce per-token allocation overhead on INT8 hotpaths; fuses dequant+transpose+requant microkernel; KV cache coalescer improves continuous-batching throughput. Measured p50 latency down 8-12% and throughput up ~18% on typical INT8 workloads. No user-facing API changes.
body:
Context and motivation:
We identified two runtime inefficiencies on our INT8/FP8 serving paths that disproportionately affect short-lived hotpath allocations and continuous batching with KV cache traffic: 1) per-token temporary scale buffers are allocated/freed frequently across lanes, increasing allocator pressure and jitter; 2) KV cache prefetches and continuous batching introduce cross-lane contention during slot alignment which prevents optimal coalescing of microbatches.

This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: an ephemeral scale allocator and a lock-free lane synchronizer. The ephemeral allocator reuses small per-request scale buffers from a per-worker ring with epoch-based reclamation (no central locks). The lane synchronizer provides a light-weight rendezvous primitive that aligns KV-prefetch windows across active lanes so the continuous batcher can merge token batches with lower overhead. In addition, we add a compact fused microkernel (fused_deq_transpose_requant) for the common path INT8->FP16 compute->INT8/FP8 fallback to eliminate intermediate copies.

What changed (single-string description with checklist):
- Implement ephemeral scale allocator with epoch reclamation and config flag: runtime.ephemeral_scale.enabled (default true)
- Add lane synchronizer primitive and integrate with continuous-batcher and kv-prefetch coordinator
- Implement fused_deq_transpose_requant microkernel (C++ + CUDA) with integer scaling LUT path for INT8
- Scheduler hints: allow scheduler to prefer "lane_coalesced" bundles when synchronizer is active
- Small API: expose internal metric keys: runtime.ephemeral_scale.reuse_rate, runtime.lane_sync.wait_ms, runtime.kv_coalesce.merge_ratio
- Unit tests for allocator and synchronizer, integration test for continuous-batcher correctness
- Bench harness updates and a perf job that collects p50/p95 latency and token throughput for INT8 workloads

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc attached (link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2042/ephemeral-scale-allocator-design)
- [x] Unit + integration tests added
- [x] Perf benchmarks run in benchmark-lab (job id: bench/2026-01-25/ephemeral-scale)
- [x] Feature gated behind runtime.ephemeral_scale.enabled and can be disabled via env var
- [x] No public API breaking changes

Commits (summary):
- 7c3a9d1 Implement ephemeral scale allocator with epoch reclamation and tests
- b1f7e44 Add lane synchronizer primitive and continuous-batcher integration
- d2e4f20 fused_deq_transpose_requant microkernel and CUDA launch wrapper
- a9f5b33 Scheduler hint plumbing + metrics export for reuse/merge ratios
- f0c8a66 Fix race in epoch reclamation under high concurrency (addressed review)
- e6b1f12 Bench harness: add INT8 hotpath scenario and perf report script

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/alloc/ephemeral_scale_allocator.{h,cpp}  (allocator core + tests)
- runtime/kv/lane_synchronizer.{h,cpp}  (rendezvous primitive)
- runtime/batching/continuous_batcher.cpp  (use lane synchronizer when enabled)
- runtime/kernels/fused_deq_transpose_requant.cu  (new microkernel)
- runtime/kernels/launcher.cpp  (kernel registration and fallback path)
- runtime/scheduler/scheduler_hints.cpp  (new enum and preference code)
- bench/benchmarks/int8_hotpath.yaml  (bench job definition)
- tests/integration/kv_coalesce_integration.test  (integration test)
- docs/ops/feature_flags.md  (document runtime.ephemeral_scale flag)

Small code excerpt (allocator usage in continuous_batcher, illustrative):
``
// reuse scale buffer from local ring; falls back to stack if disabled
auto* buf = allocator->acquire(scale_size);
apply_scale_inplace(buf, tokens);
allocator->release(buf);
```

Benchmarks (benchmark-lab; single-run median numbers):
- Workload: 2048-token long-chained chat, INT8 quantized model (gpt-like)
- Baseline (main, no allocator/sync): p50 = 42.1ms, tokens/sec = 23.4k, cost/token = 1.00x
- With changes: p50 = 37.6ms (-10.7%), tokens/sec = 27.6k (+17.9%), cost/token ~= 0.86x (-14%)
- p95 improved modestly (~6-8ms) due to reduced allocation jitter

Correctness and safety notes:
- Ephemeral allocator uses epoch-based reclamation to avoid ABA/free-after-free while remaining lock-free for the common path. Fallback path uses thread-local stack allocation for very small sizes (<64B) to avoid cross-lane contention in microbench workloads.
- The fused kernel contains a fallback path to the prior dequant->transpose->requant sequence when input shapes or alignment are not supported. A config flag runtime.kernels.fused_deq.enabled controls usage.

Review thread (high-level):
- Liam O'Connor (reviewer) 2026-01-19: "Nice microkernel. Concern: epoch reclamation loop may spin under heavy stall; prefer exponential backoff and metric for active stalls."
- Maya Chen (author) 2026-01-20: "Added backoff and a metric runtime.ephemeral_scale.backoff_count. Also added tighter unit tests that simulate stalls."
- Priya Desai (reviewer) 2026-01-21: "Please add a smoke test that runs fused kernel with FP8 fallback on CPU CI runner."
- Maya Chen 2026-01-22: "Added CPU fallback smoke test and CI job entry. Also fixed a UB on misaligned 4-byte loads reported by sanitizer."
- Diego Morales (reviewer) 2026-01-24: "Run results look good; request to add a scheduler opt-out when pod-level latency SLO is tight."
- Maya Chen 2026-01-24: "Added scheduler opt-out config runtime.scheduler.allow_lane_coalesce (default true) and surfaced note in docs."
- CI history: initial push failed lint (clang-format) and a flaky test `kv_cache_eviction.test`; both addressed in follow-up commits and all checks passed on 2026-01-27.

Performance experiments and follow-ups:
- Bench run attached: bench/2026-01-25/ephemeral-scale/report.json (internal artifact). Summary above.
- Follow-up work: extend fused kernel to support per-head quantization scale LUT (ENG-2101) and evaluate FP8-only fastpath in a subsequent PR.

Merge outcome:
- Approvals: Liam O'Connor, Priya Desai, Diego Morales
- Merge method: squash-and-merge on 2026-01-29 by Maya Chen
- Post-merge: Canary rollout to dedicated cluster pool with eps=0.1; monitored metric runtime.ephemeral_scale.reuse_rate and runtime.kv_coalesce.merge_ratio for one week; no regressions observed.

Notes for operators:
- Default is safe-on: ephemeral allocator on, fused kernel enabled only for supported shapes. To disable: set RUNTIME_EPHEMERAL_SCALE=0 and RUNTIME_KERNELS_FUSED_DEQ=0 in the agent config.
